slides.say: a and b are integers. a is odd, and b is even and not zero. Which of the following is the most precise description of six a over b squared?

Division and parity, and a trap. Six a on top is even, and b squared at the bottom is even. Even over even, and the rule says it can be anything. So choice number one? That's the trap. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, cancelling first, and then plugging in three times.
[short pause] Let's start by cancelling. b is even, so b is two k, for some integer k. Two k squared is four k squared. Six over four, cancel a two, and it's three a over two k squared.
Now three a is odd times odd, odd. And two k squared is even. Odd over even is always a fraction, because the odd top has no two to cancel the bottom's two. Choice number two is our answer.
at: Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: So in a fraction, cancel first, and only then judge. The two inside the six cancelled with a two hiding in b.

[pause] Now let's try plugging in. It's division, so three plug-ins, close together. a is one and b is two, six over four. A fraction. a is three and b is two, eighteen over four, a fraction. a is three and b is four, eighteen over sixteen, a fraction.
at: a is one and b is two
a is three and b is four

slides.say: Fraction every time. So always a fraction, choice number two. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
